identity.name: Scandinavian minor kingdoms
alt_names: Vendel Period and Viking Age Scandinavia

land.text: the Norse shape of 490-499 (358 cells), 348 of which lie inside the 500 shape

predecessors.note: Cliopatria begins this row in 500 on 378,587 km2, 1,642 cells more than the Norse row it follows.

land.text: Angeln, the Anglian homeland in southern Jutland (6 cells, 5 of them inside this row's 500 shape)

predecessors.note: The angles dossier names this row as the successor of Angeln, but this row begins in 500 and the Norse shape of 490-499 stops at 54.885N, short of Angeln: the land is nobody's 480-499 and enters the 500 shape. The angles dissolve in 479 therefore names a successor that begins only in 500 (routed to eu-06).

land.text: Schleswig, the Danish border town of Hedeby and its surroundings (20 cells inside this row's 875 shape), conquered by Henry the Fowler in 934

successors.note: Henry the Fowler page: he 'also conquered Schleswig in 934'. The page gives no extent and no end of German control. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Denmark shape of 936, which lies wholly inside this row's 875 shape, contains the same 20 cells, and the kingdom-of-germany dossier gives them back to the Danes in 936 (a bridging date, confidence 1): so the 936 Danish gain is 201 cells from this row plus these 20 from kingdom-of-germany.

land.text: Norway's petty kingdoms, 1,004 cells in 866, then Hålogaland (Nordland and Troms) in 870 and Rogaland in 872

successors.note: Cliopatria cuts Norway off in 866, Hålogaland in 870; the Harald Fairhair page dates Hafrsfjord (Rogaland) to 872.

land.text: Jutland and the islands (221 cells) in 936, then Scania, Halland and Blekinge (114 cells) in 960

successors.note: The 936 and 947 Danish shapes lie wholly inside the 935 and 947 shapes of this row. The 936 shape holds the Hedeby circle (20 cells) that this row lost to the Kingdom of Germany in 934; see the kingdom-of-germany successor.

land.text: all the land Sweden takes from this row: the Mälaren lands (136 cells) in 980, Värmland, Dalarna, Örebro, Västergötland and Östergötland (345 cells) in 1000, and the last 252 cells in 1003 (733 cells in the 979 shape)

successors.note: The 979 shape is the sum of the three handovers (136 + 345 + 252 cells). The remainder after 1000 is Småland, Öland, parts of Västergötland and Östergötland, and Gotland. The Geats page keeps the Geats 'still politically independent' in the 10th century and styled 'king of the West Geats' in the 1080s, so the 1003 absorption of the Geatish remainder is Cliopatria's, not the page's.

capitals.name: Old Uppsala (Gamla Uppsala)
capitals.note: An aggregate has no seat. The Vendel Period page: 'Old Uppsala was probably the centre of religious and political life.' Cliopatria gives Uppland and the Mälaren lands to the Kingdom of Sweden in 980 (the Eric the Victorious page: 'His original territory was in Uppland and neighbouring provinces'), so Old Uppsala lies outside this row's shapes from 980 and the capital ends in 979. No seat is documented for the residual (Småland, Gotland, parts of Götaland) 980-1002.

keyframe_review.note: 378,587 km2 (1,990 cells: Norway, Sweden, Jutland and the Danish islands), containing the whole Norse shape of 499. The Vendel Period page (c. 550-800) shows many rivals, not one state: 'great wars called the Swedish-Geatish wars between the Swedish house of Scylfling and the Geatish house of Wulfling'; its only political centre is 'Old Uppsala was probably the centre of religious and political life'. The shape is an aggregate of petty kingdoms, soft throughout. The Danes page (opened for the Norse dossier) places the Danes in Zealand and Scania from the 6th century, both inside this shape. No infobox area on either page. Unverified in detail: pages silent on a boundary.
382,454 km2: eight cells added (3 in Denmark, 3 in Sweden) against the 500 shape. Unverified: pages silent on 523. The Vendel Period page's nearest date is 'Volcanic winter of 536'.

423,261 km2: 127 cells added (67 in Norway, 30 of them in Nordland; 16 in Sweden) and 70 removed (38 in Norway, 25 in Sweden), a redrawing of the interior frontier cells. The Viking Age page: 'By 800, some 30 small kingdoms existed in Norway'; the age begins with 'the Viking attack of 8 June 793' on Lindisfarne. Unverified: no page names the cells moved in 793.

Identical to the 793 shape (423,261.0 km2, same cells). The Viking Age page: 'By 801, a strong central authority appears to have been established in Jutland', which the shape, a single aggregate, does not draw as a separate Danish state. The Eider boundary of 804 (see 806) touches the last two years of this shape.

423,409 km2; no cell differs from the 800 shape. The Gudfred page: 'In 804, a Frankish army penetrated as far as the Ejder (Eider), Denmark's southern boundary at the time.' So the strip down to the Eider (14 cells, 8.8-10.9E, 54.2-55.1N), which Cliopatria draws only from 814, is Danish already in 804: corrected as the 814 shape, applied from 804 (the 800 shape's last two years, 804-805, are not worth a keyframe). Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Franks shape holds these same cells until 813 and its ledger records a 814 loss of them to this row, so 804-813 is double-held between the two dossiers; the page makes the strip Danish, so the Frankish shape is wrong north of the Eider (routed to eu-07 in the notes).

correction.text: Denmark's southern boundary at the Eider, already in 804: 'a Frankish army penetrated as far as the Ejder (Eider), Denmark's southern boundary at the time'

keyframe_review.note: 426,175 km2: adds the Eider strip (14 cells, Schleswig south of the Schlei) to the 806 shape. The Gudfred page dates the Eider boundary to 804, not 814; see the 806 verdict and the 804 ledger gain. Hedeby, 'first mentioned in the Frankish chronicles of Einhard (804)' (Hedeby page), lies inside.

426,216 km2: not one cell differs from the 814 shape; the only change is a sliver of 41 km2 that stretches the bounding box east to 40.5E, in the Volga country. The Rus' Khaganate page puts a hypothetical khaganate 'between c. 830 and the 890s', origin of the Rus' 'in Scandinavia, possibly Sweden' ('they were Swedes', 839), and says its location 'has been actively disputed'; no page gives Scandinavian territory there. The sliver is below the grid; the neighbours list's rus and kievan-rus contacts (880-935) come from it. No effect on the map.

236,201 km2: Norway is cut away (1,004 cells removed, 938 of them in Norway, including 49 of Rogaland's cells). The Harald Fairhair page: 'In 866, Harald made the first of a series of conquests over the many petty kingdoms'; but Rogaland, Stavanger and Hafrsfjord, falls only 'In 872, after a great victory at Hafrsfjord near Stavanger against Kjotve the Rich', 'traditionally dated to 872'. Corrected: the 866 shape keeps Rogaland until 872 (the same reading as the Old Kingdom of Norway dossier, which founds the kingdom on the 866 shape without Rogaland). The same 866 sentence continues 'including Värmland in Sweden, which had sworn allegiance to the Swedish saga-king Erik Eymundsson', and the Värmland page says it 'came under Norwegian control in the late 9th and through the 10th century' (Snorri and other Icelandic sources). Cliopatria keeps Värmland (72 cells) in this row and the correction does not touch it: both pages rest on sagas, give no end, and Cliopatria's Old Kingdom of Norway never holds Värmland; it is recorded as contested 866-872 instead.

correction.text: the 866 shape plus Rogaland, which stays outside Harald's kingdom until Hafrsfjord in 872 (applies 866-869)

keyframe_review.note: 228,119 km2: Hålogaland (Nordland and Troms, 134 cells that the Old Kingdom of Norway shape gains) leaves, and 139 cells are added around Värmland and Svealand (136 in Sweden, 37 in Värmland; none belongs to Cliopatria's Norway). The Harald Fairhair page does not date Hålogaland; the 870 cut is Cliopatria's. Rogaland is again the Hafrsfjord correction: the shape keeps it until 872 (applies 870-871). The Värmland cells added in 870 run against the Harald Fairhair page, which puts Värmland among Harald's conquests of 866; they are kept because the page's account is saga-based and Cliopatria's Norway never holds them.

correction.text: the 870 shape plus Rogaland, held until Hafrsfjord in 872 (applies 870-871)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 872-874: the Cliopatria 870 shape unchanged, i.e. without Rogaland. Harald Fairhair page: 'In 872, after a great victory at Hafrsfjord near Stavanger against Kjotve the Rich', Harald became king of the whole country; the page says the battle is 'traditionally dated to 872' and rests on sagas written centuries later.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 870 shape unchanged: no Rogaland, no Hålogaland; Norway is Harald's from 872

keyframe_review.note: Applies 875-933 (the 934 keyframe below takes Schleswig out for 934-935). 228,752 km2: 10 cells added (6 in Sweden, 4 of them in Värmland; 2 in Norway) and 4 removed (3 in Norway) against the 870 shape, a frontier tidy-up. Page silent (the Viking Age page, reopened 2026-10-25, has only 'In 875, King Harald Fairhair led a fleet from Norway to Scotland'). The Hedeby page: 'A Swedish dynasty founded by Olof the Brash is said to have ruled Hedeby during the last decades of the 9th century', so Hedeby (inside the shape since 814) is held by Swedes in these decades, under the same aggregate as the Danes.

minus.text: Schleswig, conquered by Henry the Fowler in 934

correction.text: the Cliopatria 875 shape without Schleswig (the Hedeby circle, 20 cells): Henry 'also conquered Schleswig in 934'; applies 934-935

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 934-935: the 875 shape (228,752 km2) minus the 20 cells round Hedeby (about 5,058 km2). The Henry the Fowler page: he 'also conquered Schleswig in 934' and the lead says 'by conquering Danish realms in Schleswig in 934'; it gives no month, no extent and no end of German control. Cliopatria keeps Schleswig in this row to 935 and then in the Danish 936 shape; the kingdom-of-germany dossier gains it in 934 (confidence 3) and gives it to the Danes in 936. The Hedeby page is silent on 934 (it records the bishopric of 948, 'belonged to the Archbishopric of Hamburg and Bremen').

171,868 km2: Jutland and the Danish islands (221 cells, 8.1-12.5E) leave for the Kingdom of Denmark, whose 936 shape (57,037 km2) is exactly these cells. The Gorm the Old page: 'reigning from c. 936'; Harthacnut 'seized power in the early 10th century' and 'deposed the young king Sigtrygg Gnupasson, reigning over Western Denmark'; 'it is speculated that Gorm only ruled Jutland from his seat in Jelling'. The shape is Sweden only (Norway and Denmark are gone). The 221 Danish cells include the Hedeby circle (20 cells) that Henry the Fowler took in 934, so the 936 shape here is unchanged but those 20 cells had already left this row two years earlier; Cliopatria's Danish shape holds them from 936 (kingdom-of-germany loss 936, confidence 1).

145,786 km2: Scania, Halland and Blekinge (114 cells, 11.9-16.0E, 55.1-57.8N: Skåne 56, Halland 26, Blekinge 13) leave for the Kingdom of Denmark, exactly the cells the Danish 960 shape adds. The Harald Bluetooth page: reign 'c. 958 - c. 986'; the Curmsun disc 'names him king of the Danes, Scania, and Jumne', with no year for the conquest of Scania. The Scania page, opened for the repair pass: Scania 'came under Danish king Harald Bluetooth in the middle of the 10th century'; it does not date Halland or Blekinge.

117,735 km2: the Mälaren lands (136 cells: Stockholm 30, Södermanland 35, Uppsala 35, Västmanland 26) leave for the Kingdom of Sweden, whose 980 shape (27,891 km2) is exactly these cells. The Eric the Victorious page: he 'was King of Sweden as of around 970' (c. 945 - c. 995), his 'original territory was in Uppland and neighbouring provinces', 'the Swedish heartland around lake Mälaren'; the page therefore puts the Swedish kingdom on these lands about ten years before Cliopatria's 980, which is kept. The Olof Skötkonung page gives only 'He succeeded his father in c. 995'.

53,937 km2: 345 cells (Värmland 113, Västra Götaland 67, Dalarna 62, Örebro 51, Östergötland 20, Gävleborg 13, Västmanland 13) leave for the Kingdom of Sweden, whose 1000 shape (91,890 km2) adds exactly these. The Olof Skötkonung page: he was 'the first king known to have ruled both the Swedes and the Geats', 'installed a bishopric in the province of Västergötland' and was baptised 'in Husaby in Västergötland'; it dates Svolder to 1000 but not the union, so the year is Cliopatria's. The residue is Småland, Öland, Gotland and parts of Götaland. Repair pass: the Olof page adds that 'a widening of Olof's base of power around 1000' has been suggested; the Geats page has the Geats 'still politically independent' in the 10th century, with no year for the union.

ledger.note: 500: the Scandinavian minor kingdoms begin, as Cliopatria's aggregate of the Scandinavian petty kingdoms. Page silent on a founding: the Vendel Period page dates its period 'c. 550-800 AD'. The year is Cliopatria's, the year after its Norse row ends. Five of the six Angeln cells (Angles@479) lie inside this shape; Angeln is nobody's land 480-499.

region.text: Cliopatria's 500 shape: Norway, Sweden, Jutland and the Danish islands (1,990 cells), the Norse land plus the rest of Scandinavia

ledger.note: 523: a few cells are added in Denmark and southern Sweden. Page silent; the year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: the eight cells added in 523, scattered in Denmark and southern Sweden; no page names them

ledger.note: 793: the shape is redrawn at the start of the Viking Age. 'The Viking attack of 8 June 793' on Lindisfarne 'is regarded as the beginning of the Viking Age'; 'By 800, some 30 small kingdoms existed in Norway'. The page names no land gained; the 127 cells are Cliopatria's. Repair pass: the Petty kingdoms of Norway page (opened) says only that 'a number of small communities were gradually organised into larger regions in the 9th century' and that there were 'at least 9 petty realms in Western Norway during the early Viking Age'; it is silent on Nordland, Hedmark and Värmland.

region.text: the 127 cells added in 793, mostly in Norway (67, of them 30 in Nordland) and Sweden (16); no page names them

ledger.note: 793: 70 interior cells (Hedmark 25, Värmland 13) are dropped in the same redrawing. Page silent; the year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: the 70 cells removed in 793, in Norway (38), Sweden (25: Värmland 13) and Denmark (5); no page names them

ledger.note: 804: Denmark's southern boundary is the Eider. 'In 804, a Frankish army penetrated as far as the Ejder (Eider), Denmark's southern boundary at the time.' The Gudfred page (reopened 2026-10-25) does not say who held the strip before 804 or that the Franks lost it; it says only that Sliesthorp 'marked the border between Saxony and Gudfred's realm'. Cliopatria draws the strip (14 cells) from 814 and its Kingdom of the Franks shape holds it until 813, with a 814 loss to this row (kingdom-of-the-franks /ledger/91); the counterpart is named kingdom-of-the-franks so that eu-07 can move that loss to 804 or adjust its 800-813 shapes, not because the page says the Franks lost it. 804 is the latest year the strip could have been gained.

region.text: the strip down to the Eider (14 cells, 8.8-10.9E, 54.2-55.1N): 'Denmark's southern boundary at the time'

ledger.note: 808: Gudfred strikes the Obotrites. 'Gudfred resolved to attack the Obodrites in the old Saxon territories' and 'destroyed the important port Reric by the Baltic coast' (Gudfred page: the body text gives no year, its footnote cites Einhard's annals for 808); the Hedeby page: 'In 808 the Danish king Godfred (Lat. Godofredus) destroyed a competing Slav trade centre named Reric', and he resettled its merchants to Hedeby. Mirrors the obotrites dossier's contest 808-810 against this row.

region.text: the Obotrite lands: Holstein and the Baltic coast with Reric

ledger.note: 810: the Danish pressure on the Obotrites ends with Gudfred's death. He was 'murdered by one of his housecarls' (810) and 'succeeded by his nephew Hemming'; 'the new ruler concluded a peace treaty with the Franks in 811'. The page does not mention the Obotrites in connection with the peace.

region.text: the Obotrite lands

ledger.note: 866: Harald Fairhair begins the conquests that unite Norway. 'In 866, Harald made the first of a series of conquests over the many petty kingdoms.' The page gives no boundary; the region follows the Old Kingdom of Norway dossier, which founds the kingdom on this shape without Rogaland. Cliopatria cuts 1,004 cells from this row in 866. The same sentence goes on 'including Värmland in Sweden, which had sworn allegiance to the Swedish saga-king Erik Eymundsson'; Värmland is not part of this loss, see the contest below.

region.text: Vestfold and the lands Harald conquers before Hafrsfjord: Norway's 866 shape without Rogaland

ledger.note: 866: the fighting over the remaining Norwegian petty kingdoms starts with Harald's first conquests. The page: 'In 866, Harald made the first of a series of conquests over the many petty kingdoms ... including Värmland in Sweden, which had sworn allegiance to the Swedish saga-king Erik Eymundsson'; it dates no later campaign before Hafrsfjord (872). It adds that 'Harald drove Erik Eymundsson out of Värmland and inserted Áki's son Ubbi' and the Värmland page says it 'came under Norwegian control in the late 9th and through the 10th century' (sagas); Cliopatria keeps Värmland in this row, hence a contest and no loss.

region.text: the lands still outside Harald's realm: Rogaland (Stavanger, Hafrsfjord), Hålogaland, and Värmland, which the page names among the 866 conquests

ledger.note: 870: Hålogaland, the north, passes to Harald. The Harald Fairhair page does not date it; 870 is Cliopatria's shape year (the Old Kingdom of Norway dossier cites the saga line 'Namdalen and Hålogaland were in his grasp' from the same page). Repair pass: the Hålogaland page (opened) is silent on the year; 'Håkon Grjotgardsson, an earl from Hålogaland' joined Harald, undated, and Thorolf Kveldulfsson is 'tax chief starting 872 AD'.

region.text: Hålogaland (Nordland and Troms), 134 cells that Cliopatria's Old Kingdom of Norway gains in 870

ledger.note: 870: 139 cells are added in Sweden (136 in Sweden, 37 in Värmland). The year and cells are Cliopatria's; no page names them. The Harald Fairhair page puts Värmland among Harald's conquests of 866 ('including Värmland in Sweden') and has him drive out Erik Eymundsson and install the jarl Ubbi, and the Värmland page has it 'under Norwegian control in the late 9th and through the 10th century' (Snorri and other Icelandic sources), so adding Värmland cells to this row runs against both pages; Cliopatria's shape is kept because the pages rest on sagas and give no end (contest 866-872 above).

region.text: the 139 cells added in 870 around Värmland and Svealand (136 in Sweden, 37 in Värmland); none lies in Cliopatria's Norway

ledger.note: 872: Harald wins at Hafrsfjord and the west coast is his. 'In 872, after a great victory at Hafrsfjord near Stavanger against Kjotve the Rich', Harald became king of the whole country; 'traditionally dated to 872'. The page gives Stavanger; the province Rogaland is the reading. Cliopatria removes Rogaland from this row in 866.

region.text: Rogaland, the province of Stavanger and Hafrsfjord

ledger.note: 872: the wars of unification end at Hafrsfjord, after which Harald is king of the whole country. The page gives the victory, not a treaty. For Värmland the page gives no end (the Värmland page has Norwegian control through the 10th century); 872 closes the contest here as the end of the wars of unification, and Cliopatria's shape keeps Värmland in this row to 1000. Unresolved: the old-kingdom-of-norway dossier has no matching contest or vassal event for Värmland.

region.text: Rogaland, Hålogaland and Värmland; after Hafrsfjord Harald is king of the whole country

ledger.note: 875: a frontier tidy-up of 10 cells added and 4 dropped. Page silent; the Viking Age page's only 875 fact is that 'King Harald Fairhair led a fleet from Norway to Scotland'.

region.text: the 10 cells added in 875 along the Norway-Sweden frontier (6 in Sweden, 4 of them in Värmland; 2 in Norway); 4 other cells are dropped

ledger.note: 875: 4 cells (3 in Norway) are dropped in the same frontier tidy-up as the 10 added above. Page silent; the Viking Age page (reopened) has only 'In 875, King Harald Fairhair led a fleet from Norway to Scotland'. The year and cells are Cliopatria's.

region.text: the 4 cells dropped in 875, 3 of them in Norway; no page names them

ledger.note: 934: Henry the Fowler conquers Schleswig from the Danes. Henry 'also conquered Schleswig in 934' and the lead says 'by conquering Danish realms in Schleswig in 934' (Henry the Fowler page). The year and the land are the page's; the extent (a 40 km circle round Hedeby, 20 cells inside this row's 875 shape) is the researcher's reading, as in the kingdom-of-germany dossier, which gains it at confidence 3. The page gives no end of German control; Cliopatria's Danish shape holds Schleswig again from 936.

region.text: Schleswig, the Danish border town of Hedeby and its surroundings: 'also conquered Schleswig in 934'

ledger.note: 936: Gorm the Old becomes king and Denmark leaves the minor kingdoms. 'reigning from c. 936'; he 'ruled from Jelling'. The year is the page's ('c. 936'); the page speculates that Gorm 'only ruled Jutland', so the islands in the shape are Cliopatria's. The other 20 cells of Cliopatria's Danish shape lie round Hedeby, which Henry the Fowler took in 934; the Danes hold them again from 936 in Cliopatria (kingdom-of-germany loss 936, confidence 1), which the Kingdom of Denmark dossier should gain from kingdom-of-germany.

region.text: Jutland and the Danish islands without the Hedeby circle already lost in 934: 201 of the 221 cells of Cliopatria's Kingdom of Denmark of 936

ledger.note: 960: Scania and the Swedish south-west pass to the Danes. The Scania page: Scania 'came under Danish king Harald Bluetooth in the middle of the 10th century'; the Harald Bluetooth page: reign 'c. 958 - c. 986' and the Curmsun disc 'names him king of the Danes, Scania, and Jumne'. 960 is Cliopatria's year inside the page's 'middle of the 10th century'; the Scania page does not date Halland or Blekinge, which come with it in Cliopatria's shape.

region.text: Scania, Halland and Blekinge, 114 cells (Skåne 56, Halland 26, Blekinge 13)

ledger.note: 980: Cliopatria starts the Kingdom of Sweden on the Mälaren lands. The Eric the Victorious page: he 'was King of Sweden as of around 970', his 'original territory was in Uppland and neighbouring provinces' and 'the Swedish heartland around lake Mälaren'; he founded Sigtuna 'in all probability'. 980 is Cliopatria's year, about ten years after the page's.

region.text: the Mälaren lands, 136 cells (Uppsala, Stockholm, Södermanland, Västmanland)

ledger.note: 1000: the Geats and the middle lands join the Kingdom of Sweden. Olof Skötkonung was 'the first king known to have ruled both the Swedes and the Geats'; he 'installed a bishopric in the province of Västergötland'; 'a widening of Olof's base of power around 1000' has been suggested, and the Battle of Svolder was fought in '999 or 1000'. The Geats page has the Geats 'still politically independent' in the 10th century. The page does not date the union, so the year 1000 is Cliopatria's, supported only as 'around 1000'.

region.text: Värmland, Dalarna, Örebro, Västergötland, Östergötland, Gävleborg and Västmanland: 345 cells

ledger.note: 1002: the last minor kingdoms join the Kingdom of Sweden, whose 1003 shape is 144,672 km2. Page silent on 1002; it says 'the construction of a Swedish kingdom was a long process that was only concluded in the 13th century'. The Geats page (opened) keeps the Geats a separate people in the 1080s ('king of the West Geats') and has no year for their union with the Swedes.

region.text: the last 252 cells: Småland, Öland, Gotland, and parts of Västergötland and Östergötland

wars.name: Gudfred's wars against the Franks and the Obotrites

zones.text: the strip down to the Eider (14 cells): 'Denmark's southern boundary at the time' (804)
the Obotrite lands in the old Saxon territories, with Reric

wars.outcome: A Frankish army reached the Eider in 804, which is Denmark's southern boundary; Gudfred destroyed Reric in 808 and the Slavic lands accepted Danish overlordship until Drożko's return and murder in the rebuilt Reric; Gudfred was murdered in 810 while Charlemagne planned a major expedition against him, and his successor made peace with the Franks in 811.
wars.note: 'In 804, a Frankish army penetrated as far as the Ejder (Eider), Denmark's southern boundary at the time'; 'Gudfred resolved to attack the Obodrites in the old Saxon territories'; 'In 810 Charlemagne stayed at his main residence in Aachen, drawing up plans for a major military expedition against Gudfred'; 'the new ruler concluded a peace treaty with the Franks in 811'. The Eider strip is the 804 ledger gain; the Obotrite zone is the contest 808-810, mirroring the obotrites dossier. The 808 date of Reric is the Gudfred page's footnote and the Hedeby page's.

wars.name: Harald Fairhair's wars of unification

zones.text: Rogaland (Hafrsfjord, near Stavanger), Hålogaland and Värmland, the lands still outside Harald's realm

wars.outcome: Harald wins the Battle of Hafrsfjord in 872 and becomes king of the whole country; the petty kingdoms of Norway leave the minor kingdoms for the Old Kingdom of Norway. Värmland, which the page counts among the 866 conquests, stays in Cliopatria's minor kingdoms shape.
wars.note: The page: 'In 866, Harald made the first of a series of conquests over the many petty kingdoms'; 'In 872, after a great victory at Hafrsfjord near Stavanger against Kjotve the Rich'. The dates rest on sagas written centuries later and the page notes that some historians doubt Harald existed.

wars.name: Henry the Fowler's Danish campaign

zones.text: Schleswig, the Danish border town of Hedeby and its surroundings

wars.outcome: Henry the Fowler conquers Schleswig from the Danes in 934; the page gives neither the extent nor the end of German control, and Cliopatria holds Schleswig again in the Danish shape of 936.
wars.note: 'also conquered Schleswig in 934'; 'by conquering Danish realms in Schleswig in 934'; 'Henry also pacified territories to the north, where the Danes had been harrying the Frisians by sea'. The page gives no month and no battle.

wars.name: Battle of Svolder
wars.outcome: Olaf Tryggvason of Norway is attacked by 'the allied fleets' at Svolder; the victors divide Norway, Olof Skötkonung receiving parts of Trøndelag and Bohuslän.
wars.note: 'Olaf Tryggvason was attacked by the allied fleets in the Battle of Svolder'; the page dates it '999 or 1000' (Snorri: 1000), and from and to are kept at 1000. Listed for completeness: the Norwegian shares are not part of this row's land (Cliopatria has this row as southern Sweden by 1000), and the Old Kingdom of Norway dossier carries the Danish overlordship of Viken after 1000.

certainty.note: An aggregate of petty kingdoms: 'By 800, some 30 small kingdoms existed in Norway'. No border is fixed by treaty or survey; the least soft edge is the Danish southern boundary at the Eider ('Denmark's southern boundary at the time', 804), and the Danevirke that Gudfred strengthened, still soft.

notes: Scandinavian minor kingdoms is a Cliopatria aggregate (Wikidata Q1275225 for the Vendel Period, Q213649 for the Viking Age; the dossier keeps the first, the schema holds one id; Seshat id sv_scandinavian_minor_k, not opened) for every Scandinavian petty kingdom from 500 to 1002. It is not a state: the pages show 'some 30 small kingdoms' in Norway by 800 and rival Swedish and Geatish houses; type is state only because the schema has no word for an aggregate. The row breaks into its successors cell for cell: Norway from 866 (Old Kingdom of Norway), Denmark in 936 and 960 (Kingdom of Denmark, 221 + 114 cells, exactly the Danish shapes) and Sweden in 980, 1000 and 1003 (Kingdom of Sweden, 136 + 345 + 252 cells, which add up to the Swedish shapes within 15 cells). Shape remarks: the 825 shape differs from the 814 shape by 41 km2 only (a sliver to 40.5E that touches no cell), which is the source of the neighbours list's rus (880-881) and kievan-rus (882-935) contacts; the 800, 806 and 825 shapes change no cell. The page budget (9 pages) was spent and the repair pass reopened Vendel Period, Viking Age, Petty kingdoms of Norway, Hålogaland and Värmland: the 523, 793 and 875 cell changes and the 870 addition of 139 Swedish cells in Värmland and Svealand are still explained by no page (confidence 1 events); the 875 drop of 4 cells now has its own loss event. The Harald Fairhair page puts Värmland in its 866 sentence ('including Värmland in Sweden, which had sworn allegiance to the Swedish saga-king Erik Eymundsson') and says Harald 'drove Erik Eymundsson out of Värmland and inserted Áki's son Ubbi'; the Värmland page has it 'under Norwegian control in the late 9th and through the 10th century' (sagas); Cliopatria keeps Värmland in this row until 1000 and adds 37 more Värmland cells in 870. Kept against the pages, recorded as contested 866-872 with the Old Kingdom of Norway (whose dossier has no matching event); a vassal or loss reading from 866 would need a regain by Sweden in 1000. Rogaland: Cliopatria removes it in 866 with the rest of Norway but the page dates Hafrsfjord, Stavanger, to 872, so the 866 and 870 shapes are adjusted to keep it until 872 and an 872 keyframe is added; the Old Kingdom of Norway dossier (another group) reads the page the same way (found on the 866 shape without Rogaland, Rogaland gained 872). Hålogaland leaves in 870 in both dossiers; no page dates it. Danes: the minor kingdoms hold all of Denmark until 935. The pages opened give the Danish kings only from 804 (Gudfred, a 'ninth century Danish king who reigned from at least 804 to 810'), so no ruler list is given. The Danevirke, Hedeby and the Swedish dynasty of Olof the Brash at Hedeby (last decades of the 9th century, 'is said to') are not separate states here. Wars omitted for lack of a page: the Swedish-Geatish wars (undated), the Danish expulsion of the Heruli (6th century), Otto II's invasion of Denmark (974, belongs to the Kingdom of Denmark dossier). Counterparts: old-kingdom-of-norway, kingdom-of-denmark, kingdom-of-sweden and kingdom-of-the-franks have rows (eu-14, eu-07); the Saxons (500-799), Obotrites (793-935) and East Franks (850-910) touch the shape by Cliopatria's neighbours list but no opened page records a gain or loss against them. Gazetteer names needed: Old Uppsala (Gamla Uppsala), a place at 59.90N 17.63E, used only as a capital. Pages not opened (budget): Svear, Geats, Danevirke, Jelling, Ynglings, Kingdom of Sweden, Denmark in the Viking Age, the Seshat page. Repair pass of 2026-10-25: (1) 934 Schleswig: the Henry the Fowler page has Henry 'also conquered Schleswig in 934'; this row now has the 934 loss to kingdom-of-germany, a keyframe 934-935 (the 875 shape without the Hedeby circle, 20 cells) and a war; the Danish 936 shape contains the circle, so the 936 loss here is 201 cells and the Danes' 20 Hedeby cells come from kingdom-of-germany. (2) Eider strip: counterpart changed from nobody to kingdom-of-the-franks (Cliopatria's Frankish shape holds the strip to 813); eu-07 should move kingdom-of-the-franks /ledger/91 to 804 or adjust its 800-813 shapes. (3) Obotrites: contest 808-810 mirrored, war widened. (4) Angles named as predecessor (Angeln, nobody's 480-499); eu-06 should fix the successor year in the angles dissolve. (5) Old Uppsala ends 979. (6) Svolder '999 or 1000'. (7) The Kingdom of Sweden successor land is the 979 shape. (8) Scania (960) and the Eric the Victorious page (980) raise two handovers to confidence 2; the 1000 handover is 'around 1000' on the Olof page.
